extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and research organisations applying to the MRC/UKRI for funding
extracted.subtask_description: Lists and describes the types of funding the MRC offers (scheme types, scope, typical review mechanisms and target applicants) to help applicants choose appropriate funding routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher-led
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular, continuous funding opportunities. Proposals are reviewed at board and panel meetings. Funding is available for any area of science relevant to the MRC, to eligible groups and individuals, offering funding on a range of scales, across career stages, from fundamental to translational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use researcher‑led schemes when the research question is driven by the investigator rather than being constrained to a strategic MRC‑defined priority. Expect standard board/panel review processes and eligibility checks; suitable for a wide range of project sizes and career stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRC strategic
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding opportunities in a specific research area defined by MRC, usually for a one-off opportunity or a time‑limited period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals may have special application and review mechanisms. Apply to strategic calls when your project aligns with an MRC‑identified priority or time‑limited challenge rather than open researcher‑initiated agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutes, units and centres support
rubrics_metrics.description: We also support research through our institutes, units and centres. Some are highly focused on specific science areas overseen by a board or panel, others have a very broad research remit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding and support may be channelled via established MRC institutes/units/centres; these entities can offer thematic or broad remit programmes and may have their own governance and application pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Focused research projects that may be short or long term in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical scheme for investigator‑led projects addressing specific scientific questions. Choose this for discrete project funding; expect scheme‑specific application requirements and peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports novel partnerships between diverse groupings of researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to fund collaborative, multi‑group projects. Highlight novelty in partnership composition and clear added value from collaboration when applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Investigator Award
rubrics_metrics.description: For early career researchers who are ready to become independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at researchers transitioning to independence; applications should demonstrate readiness to lead an independent programme, appropriate support, and career development plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRC Industry Collaboration Framework (ICF)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICF supports applicants submitting collaborative research projects between academic and industry researchers. The ICF replaced the MRC Industry Collaboration Agreement (MICA) process and applies to all opportunities opening after 27 April 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ICF for academic–industry collaborative proposals. Note the procedural change (replacement of MICA) and the effective date; expect terms and collaborative arrangements governed by the ICF guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRC Centre of Research Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge‑led and time‑limited investments that tackle complex and multidisciplinary or interdisciplinary health challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate for large, challenge‑focused programmes requiring multidisciplinary collaboration and a defined time horizon. Applications should articulate how the centre will address complex health challenges and deliver coordinated research activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career awards (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: MRC provides career awards to scientists (mentioned alongside research grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad category supporting individual career progression (e.g., fellowships, development awards). Applicants should check specific scheme pages for eligibility, aims, and application details.
